findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; FlagSqlExpressions is a dead no-op
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then returns `false` from both the `if` branch and the fallthrough, so the computed value is never used and SQL expressions are disabled unconditionally. The PR description says the `FlagSqlExpressions` toggle is intentionally kept, yet this code makes it a no-op: turning the flag on will not re-enable the feature, and the dead `enabled` computation plus the negated flag read make the code look like a mistake or a polarity bug. Either return `false` directly (dropping the flag reference) if this is a permanent hard-disable, or use the flag value if the toggle is supposed to remain functional. Leaving it as-is invites a future maintainer to 'fix' the polarity and re-open the vulnerability.

findings.title: No regression test proving SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This is a security fix that disables the SQL expression query type, but no test is added or updated to assert that a `type: sql` expression is now rejected by `ReadQuery` (and by `NewSQLCommand`). Additionally, the new `pkg/expr/sql` DB stub makes `TablesList`/`RunCommands`/`QueryFramesInto` unconditionally return 'not implemented', so any existing tests in `pkg/expr` that build or execute SQL expressions will fail unless they are updated. Without a dedicated test, a later change that re-enables the SQL query type or restores a real in-memory DB would not be caught by CI. Add a test that an SQL expression query is rejected.

findings.title: Misleading error text 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'
findings.body: When the SQL query type is encountered, the code returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. The feature is not unimplemented; it is intentionally disabled to close CVE-2024-9264. Users with saved SQL-expression panels (and anyone debugging support cases) will read 'not implemented' as a bug or an unfinished feature rather than a deliberate security removal. Use a message that states the feature is disabled, e.g. `"SQL expressions are disabled"`.
